title: Unissued records, the single-day session, and founding the musicians' union
summary: Albert says Frank Driggs found an unissued record and the session was done in one day while his band was at the dinner club; he recalls being a charter member of the union, begun about 1924-25 at St. Catherine Church.

story.theme_name: The musicians' union: cards, locals, and the Black-white merger
story.community_name: The musicians' union: cards, scale and the black-white merger

blocks.x: So that we'll have that ready.
Which Frank Driggs found out here. I think I sent that thing to Frank. He asked me for it and I sent it to him.
No, with your own band or anything?
I thought you meant to say it was never issued or something.
I don't think so. I don't think so. In fact, I can't remember. When they came to record this, my band was at the Alma's Dinner Club. And that's where we went from there. It was one session all day.
Well, I'm just checking to see if it's picking up your voice. What about the founding of the union here? You were a charter member?

This thing began, I think about 1924 or 25. I can't remember the exact date. But I do remember it was over here at this old St. Catherine Church. The hall in the back. Well, the Wabash Blues just started now. I understand that I hear it. Yeah. That's the same personnel on this record that was on the others. Mm-hmm.
